findings.meaning: +0x4 = routine_0 = the state-table index into 0x8010C830 (established table). +0x5/+0x6/+0x7 are routine_1/2/3, all written together by `sw ...,4(ent)`. The EXE damage router picks HURT vs DEATH purely on the post-damage HP halfword at +0x156 (342): `bgez` -> state 2 (HURT), else state 3 (DEATH). NOTE the delay slot: `sw v0,4(s1)` at 0x80047288 stores 2 UNCONDITIONALLY, and the DEATH path then overwrites it with 3 at 0x80047290. Because the word store is used, entering HURT also zeroes +0x5/+0x6/+0x7 — which is why every reaction begins at phase 0.

verdict.why:
The claim's CORE is correct and I independently re-derived it, but it is tagged PROVEN while carrying three unproven/false riders. Since one is contradicted by an instruction, refuted=true.

== WHAT I CONFIRMED (re-disassembled + byte-verified) ==
1. State index = entity+0x4, table 0x8010C830. VERIFIED:
     801004cc: lbu v0,4(s0)          <- BYTE load of +0x4
     801004d4: sll v0,v0,2
     801004e0: lw v0,-14288(at)      at=0x80110000 -> 0x80110000-0x37D0 = 0x8010C830
     801004e8: jalr v0
     801004ec: addu a0,s0,zero       <- delay slot, a0 = entity
   Table bytes @0x8010c830: `5c 06 10 80 4c 11 10 80 40 4f 10 80 50 82 10 80` -> [0]0x8010065C [1]0x8010114C [2]0x80104F40 [3]0x80108250. HURT=2 confirmed.
2. The DELAY-SLOT reading is EXACTLY right. Bytes @0x8004727c: `56 01 23 86 | 02 00 02 24 | 03 00 61 04 | 04 00 22 ae | 03 00 02 24 | 04 00 22 ae`
     8004727c: lh v1,342(s1)      (0x86230156 -> LH +0x156)
     80047280: addiu v0,zero,2
     80047284: bgez v1,0x80047294
     80047288: sw v0,4(s1)        <- delay slot, stores 2 UNCONDITIONALLY. Correct.
     8004728c: addiu v0,zero,3
     80047290: sw v0,4(s1)
   HP>=0 -> 2 (HURT), HP<0 -> 3 (DEATH). Correct.
3. s1 really is the damaged entity: `800471fc: addu s1,s0,zero`, s0 = enemy from the list at 0x800d3c34 (`8004711c: lw s0,0(s2)`; loop `8004740c: addiu s2,s2,4` / `80047418: bne s2,v0,0x8004711c`). Function prologue = 0x800470C0.
4. +0x156 is HP: `80047258: lhu v0,342(s1)` / `80047260: subu v0,v0,v1` (v1 = dmg & 0x3ff) / `80047268: sh v0,342(s1)`, then signed re-read + bgez.
5. Bonus corroboration the claim missed: a SECOND identical site exists at 0x800474A0-0x800474B4 (same bgez/delay-slot pattern), reached when the 0x80047210 gate `beq v0,zero,0x80047434` (v0 = s5 & 0x10000) takes the other branch. So the cited site is one of two, but the HURT/DEATH rule is identical at both.

== FAILURE 1 (FALSE): "re-entered every frame while +0x4==2" ==
The dispatcher re-CALLS 0x80104F40 each frame, but HURT is NOT re-entered/re-initialized — it resumes from a PERSISTENT phase. Inside HURT:
     80104fe0: lhu a0,270(s1)        +0x10E
     80104fe8: andi v0,a0,0x1
     80104fec: beq v0,zero,0x80105014
     80104ff0: addu a1,s2,zero       <- delay slot
     80104ff4: lbu v0,5(s1)          <- reads PERSISTENT +0x5
     80104ffc: sll v0,v0,2
     80105008: lw v0,-13336(at)      -> 0x8010CBE8 (SECOND dispatch table)
     8010500c: j 0x8010540c
     80105010: addu a0,s1,zero       <- delay slot
and `8010505c: lbu v0,6(s1)` / `80105064: bne v0,zero,0x80105168` reads persistent +0x6. A state that dispatches on its own stored phase bytes is a resumed state, not one re-entered each frame. The entry (the zeroing sw) happens ONCE, in the EXE at damage time. The claim's own MEANING paragraph ("every reaction begins at phase 0") contradicts its summary sentence.

== FAILURE 2 (CONTRADICTED BY AN INSTRUCTION): "entering HURT zeroes +0x5.. which is why every reaction begins at phase 0" ==
On the (+0x10E & 1) != 0 branch, phase 0 is a NULL POINTER, called with NO guard:
     0x8010cbe8 bytes: `00 00 00 00 88 78 10 80`  -> [0] = 0x00000000, [1..15] = 0x80107888
     80105410: jalr v0              (bytes `09 f8 40 00`)
     80105414: addu a2,s3,zero      <- delay slot
There is no null check between the table load at 0x80105008 and the jalr at 0x80105410. If +0x5 were 0 on that branch, the game would `jalr 0`. Therefore "every reaction begins at phase 0" is NOT a proven consequence; something must set +0x5 nonzero on that path, and the claim never identifies that writer. UNKNOWN — needs the +0x5 writer between the damage store and the next HURT tick.

== FAILURE 3 (UNSUPPORTED INVENTION): "+0x7 = routine_3" ==
I disassembled the whole overlay (13000 instructions from 0x80100000) and grepped: there are ZERO lb/lbu/sb accesses at offset 7 anywhere in EMZ0.BIN (+0x6: 216 accesses, +0x5: 104). Nothing in this overlay gives +0x7 any meaning. Per the no-guessing rule this must be marked UNKNOWN, not asserted as routine_3.

== EVIDENCE THE CLAIM MISSED THAT ACTUALLY STRENGTHENS THE WORD MODEL ==
HURT itself writes the whole routine word, and with a NONZERO upper byte:
     801050a4: addiu v0,zero,1281   (bytes `01 05 02 24`, 1281 = 0x0501)
     801050a8: jal 0x80015fe8       (PRNG)
     801050ac: sw v0,4(s1)          <- delay slot, stores 0x00000501 BEFORE the jal target runs
Little-endian: +0x4=0x01 (ACTIVE), +0x5=0x05, +0x6=0, +0x7=0. So the routine word demonstrably carries a nonzero phase; the zeroing at 0x80047288 is a property of the value 2, not of "word stores always zero the phase". Also `801050c8: sb v0,547(s1)` with v0 = (PRNG & 0xf) + 16 -> +0x223 = 16..31, set on the same path.
verdict.correction:
CORRECTED STATEMENT (PROVEN parts only):

+0x4 is the state index (routine_0), loaded as a BYTE and used as a word index into the state table 0x8010C830:
  801004cc: lbu v0,4(s0) / 801004d4: sll v0,v0,2 / 801004e0: lw v0,-14288(at) [at=0x80110000 -> 0x8010C830] / 801004e8: jalr v0 / 801004ec: addu a0,s0,zero (delay slot)
State 2 = HURT = 0x80104F40 (table bytes @0x8010c838: `40 4f 10 80`).

The EXE hit loop (function @0x800470C0, entity s1 = s0 from the enemy list @0x800d3c34 via `800471fc: addu s1,s0,zero`) applies damage to the HP halfword at +0x156 and then selects the reaction by the SIGN of the post-damage HP:
  80047258: lhu v0,342(s1) / 80047260: subu v0,v0,v1 (v1 = dmg & 0x3ff) / 80047268: sh v0,342(s1)
  8004727c: lh v1,342(s1) / 80047280: addiu v0,zero,2 / 80047284: bgez v1,0x80047294 / 80047288: sw v0,4(s1) [DELAY SLOT - stores 2 unconditionally] / 8004728c: addiu v0,zero,3 / 80047290: sw v0,4(s1)
  => HP >= 0 -> routine word = 2 (HURT); HP < 0 -> overwritten with 3 (DEATH).
An identical second site exists at 0x800474A0-0x800474B4, selected by the gate `80047210: beq v0,zero,0x80047434` (v0 = s5 & 0x10000). Both use the same HP-sign rule.

Because the store is a WORD, writing 2 also clears +0x5/+0x6 (little-endian). This is a property of the VALUE 2, not of word stores in general - HURT itself stores 0x0501 the same way (`801050a4: addiu v0,zero,1281` / `801050ac: sw v0,4(s1)` in the delay slot of `801050a8: jal 0x80015fe8`), i.e. +0x4=1 (ACTIVE), +0x5=5.

DO NOT claim "HURT is re-entered every frame". The dispatcher re-CALLS 0x80104F40 every frame, but HURT RESUMES from persistent phase bytes: `80104ff4: lbu v0,5(s1)` feeding a second dispatch table at 0x8010CBE8 (`80105008: lw v0,-13336(at)`), and `8010505c: lbu v0,6(s1)` / `80105064: bne v0,zero,0x80105168`. Port it as "call the state handler each frame; it resumes at +0x5/+0x6", NOT as "re-initialize on every frame".

MARK AS UNKNOWN (do not invent):
 - Whether phase 0 is a valid HURT start on the (+0x10E & 1)!=0 branch. Sub-table entry [0] @0x8010CBE8 is 0x00000000 and `80105410: jalr v0` has NO null guard, so +0x5 must be nonzero by the time that branch runs. The writer that sets it has not been found. Needs: locate the +0x5 writer between the EXE damage store and the next HURT tick (check 0x800472a0-0x80047400 and the ACTIVE/state-4 EXE handler 0x80065C88).
 - The meaning of +0x7. There are ZERO byte accesses at offset 7 in the entire EMZ0.BIN overlay; calling it "routine_3" is unsupported here.

findings.title: HURT @0x80104F40 has NO decision table — it is a 2D EXECUTOR table [routine_1][+0x1D2], stride 9 words
findings.meaning: addr = 0x8010C940 + 36*ent[0x5] + 4*ent[0x1D2]. Row = routine_1 (the reaction id the EXE stamped from the attack word). Column = ent[0x1D2] (hit-zone + 3*weapon-class, see separate finding). There is NO decision/executor pair like ACTIVE has — a single executor table, and no NULL check before `jalr`. Row 0 (0x8010C940..0x8010C963) is NOT pointers (0x8032008c, 0x803e0096, 0x80480096, 0x8046006e, 0x804a0078, 0x802200b4, 0x8034006e, 0x804200c8, 0x804200b4) — it is data, so routine_1==0 would jump into garbage; reaction id 0 must never occur. The last word of row 18 (0x8010CBE8) is shared with the crawler table's NULL entry [0].

verdict.why:
VERIFIED-CORRECT PARTS (re-disassembled independently, all match): the stanza 0x801053d8-0x80105414 is verbatim accurate. `801053ec: sll v0,v1,3` + `801053f0: addu v0,v0,v1` + `801053f4: sll v0,v0,2` = *36 (9 words) PROVEN; `801053f8: lbu v1,466(a0)` = +0x1D2 and `80105400: sll v1,v1,2` = *4 PROVEN; `801053e4: lui a2,0x8011` + `801053e8: addiu a2,a2,-14016` = 0x8010C940 PROVEN; `801053e0: lbu v1,5(a0)` = row index PROVEN. So addr = 0x8010C940 + 36*ent[0x5] + 4*ent[0x1D2] is CORRECT. Row 0's nine words are exactly as listed (raw read 0x8010C940: 8032008c 803e0096 80480096 8046006e 804a0078 802200b4 8034006e 804200c8 804200b4) and lie outside PSX RAM (0x8032008c > 0x801FFFFF), so "not code pointers" is CORRECT. Row18col8 = 0x8010C940+36*18+32 = 0x8010CBE8 = crawler base, value 00000000 -- CORRECT. No NULL check on the upright path (`80105408: lw v0,0(v1)` / `8010540c: nop` / `80105410: jalr v0`) -- CORRECT. And I found no decision/executor PAIR in HURT (selection is an inlined compare-chain at 0x80105188-0x8010522c calling 0x80106128/0x80106310/0x8010640c/0x80106510), so "no decision table" survives.

FAILURE 1 (decisive) -- "There is NO decision/executor pair like ACTIVE has -- A SINGLE EXECUTOR TABLE" is FALSE. HURT dispatches through TWO different tables. Before reaching 0x801053d8 it tests +0x10E bit 0 and takes a separate 1-D table:
  80104fe0: lhu a0,270(s1)        ; ent[0x10E]
  80104fe4: nop
  80104fe8: andi v0,a0,0x1
  80104fec: beq v0,zero,0x80105014 ; bit0 clear -> upright path
  80104ff0: addu a1,s2,zero        ; DELAY SLOT (arg a1, executes on BOTH paths)
  80104ff4: lbu v0,5(s1)           ; ent[0x5]
  80104ff8: nop
  80104ffc: sll v0,v0,2            ; *4  <-- stride 4, NOT 36
  80105000: lui at,0x8011
  80105004: addu at,at,v0
  80105008: lw v0,-13336(at)       ; 0x8010CBE8 + 4*ent[0x5]
  8010500c: j 0x8010540c            ; jumps straight to the SHARED jalr
  80105010: addu a0,s1,zero        ; DELAY SLOT (arg a0)
This is the crawler variant, exactly mirroring ACTIVE's +0x10E upright/crawling split. Table @0x8010CBE8 = [0]=00000000, [1..18]=0x80107888. The claim even cites 0x8010CBE8 but only as "the crawler table's NULL entry [0]" -- it saw the second table and still described HURT as having one. A port written from this claim sends crawling zombies through the 2-D table and calls the wrong handler.

FAILURE 2 -- the NULL/risk analysis is materially wrong. The claim asserts only row 0 is dangerous ("reaction id 0 must never occur"). In fact 63 of 171 cells are genuine 0x00000000: rows 5, 6 and 17 are ENTIRELY NULL (raw reads 0x8010C9F4, 0x8010CA18, 0x8010CBA4 = 36 zero bytes each), and columns 2/5/8 are NULL in rows 1,2,3,4,7,8,12,13,14,15,16,18. With the (correctly identified) absence of a NULL check, all of those `jalr` to address 0 -- as does crawler[0]. The claim's "row 0 is the only landmine" framing is false. Note also that this 9-wide NULL periodicity is far stronger evidence for the 9-word stride than the shift chain the claim relied on, and it was missed.

FAILURE 3 -- unsupported MEANING presented as PROVEN. "Row = routine_1 (the reaction id the EXE stamped from the attack word)" has NO citation. +0x5 is the ESTABLISHED sub_state_1, the same field ACTIVE's DECISION/EXECUTOR tables index. It is written by OVERLAY code, not demonstrably by the EXE: `80102744: sb v0,5(s3)` plus twelve stores at 0x8010a4e0/0x8010a5d0/0x8010a628/0x8010a63c/0x8010a698/0x8010a6b8/0x8010a6d8/0x8010a6f0/0x8010a7b0/0x8010a7dc/0x8010a804/0x8010a808 (`sb ..,5(s0)`). HURT itself never writes +0x5. No "attack word" is cited anywhere. This must be UNKNOWN. Likewise "Column = ent[0x1D2] (hit-zone + 3*weapon-class)" is deferred to another finding and is NOT proven here; what IS provable in HURT is only a mod-3 decomposition at 0x801050b0-0x801050e4 (`lbu a0,466(s1)` / `lui v1,0xaaaa` / `ori v1,v1,0xaaab` / `multu a0,v1` / `mfhi t0` / `srl v1,t0,1` / `sll v0,v1,1` / `addu v0,v0,v1` / `subu a0,a0,v0` => a0 = ent[0x1D2] % 3), which is consistent with base-3 packing but does NOT establish which component is the low digit.

FAILURE 4 (porting-relevant precision) -- the quoted stanza is not a single linear entry. Three branches enter it at DIFFERENT offsets because their delay slots pre-set the args: `8010528c: bne v0,zero,0x801053dc` / delay `80105290: addu a0,s1,zero` (enters at 0x801053dc); `8010529c: bgez v0,0x801053e0` / delay `801052a0: addu a1,s2,zero` (enters at 0x801053e0); `801052b0: beq v0,zero,0x801053d8` / delay `801052b4: addiu a0,zero,9` (enters at 0x801053d8, where a0=9 is immediately overwritten by `addu a0,s1,zero` -- that delay slot is the arg for the fall-through `801052b8: jal 0x8005bd6c`). Many HURT paths never dispatch at all, leaving via `j 0x80105418` at 0x80105034, 0x80105114, 0x8010515c, 0x80105280 and `bne v1,v0,0x80105418` at 0x8010522c. All delay slots I checked are correctly handled by the claim where it quoted them (`80105410: jalr v0` / `80105414: addu a2,s3,zero` is right), but the single-stanza presentation hides the multi-entry structure.

VERDICT: the address arithmetic is reusable, but the structural characterization ("a single executor table"), the NULL-safety analysis, and the semantic labeling of the row index are all wrong or uncited. STATUS "PROVEN" is not warranted.
verdict.correction:
HURT @0x80104F40 has NO decision table (PROVEN -- selection logic is an inlined compare-chain at 0x80105188-0x8010522c), but it has TWO executor tables, not one, selected by +0x10E bit 0 exactly like ACTIVE's upright/crawling split:

(A) CRAWLING (ent[0x10E] & 1) != 0 -- 1-D table, stride 4:
    handler = *(u32*)(0x8010CBE8 + 4*ent[0x5])
    gate+load @0x80104fe0-0x80105008 (`andi v0,a0,0x1` / `beq v0,zero,0x80105014` delay `addu a1,s2,zero`; `lbu v0,5(s1)` / `sll v0,v0,2` / `lw v0,-13336(at)`), then `8010500c: j 0x8010540c` delay `80105010: addu a0,s1,zero` into the shared jalr.
    Contents: [0]=NULL, [1..18]=0x80107888.

    handler = *(u32*)(0x8010C940 + 36*ent[0x5] + 4*ent[0x1D2])
    @0x801053e0-0x80105408, called at `80105410: jalr v0` delay `80105414: addu a2,s3,zero`.

The meaning of +0x1D2 is likewise not established here; HURT only proves it is decomposed mod 3 at 0x801050b0-0x801050e4 (0xAAAAAAAB reciprocal divide by 3), consistent with a base-3 packing of two 0..2 fields but not identifying which is the low digit.

verdict.why:
REFUTED. The 51 raw table words the claim dumped are byte-accurate — I re-read all of them and they match. But the claim is labelled PROVEN, and both its ROW-7 spec and essentially its entire MEANING section fail.

=== FAILURE 1 (hard byte-true data error): row 7 is wrong/underspecified ===
Claim: "row7 = [0x80107438, 0x801066fc, NULL]" — no cols 3-8 given, and no "x3" marker (the claim uses "x3" elsewhere for uniform rows, so this reads as a complete 3-col row or as an implicitly uniform one; either reading is wrong).
Actual raw bytes I read myself:
  8010ca3c: 38 74 10 80  fc 66 10 80  00 00 00 00  38 74 10 80
  8010ca4c: c0 5b 10 80  00 00 00 00  38 74 10 80  38 54 10 80
  8010ca5c: 00 00 00 00
=> row7 = [7438, 66fc, NULL | 7438, 5bc0, NULL | 7438, **5438**, NULL]
Compare row8:
  8010ca60: 38 74 10 80  fc 66 10 80  00 00 00 00  38 74 10 80
  8010ca70: c0 5b 10 80  00 00 00 00  38 74 10 80  c0 5b 10 80
  8010ca80: 00 00 00 00
=> row8 = [7438, 66fc, NULL | 7438, 5bc0, NULL | 7438, **5bc0**, NULL]
Rows 7 and 8 differ in EXACTLY ONE cell: col7 (0x8010ca58 = 0x80105438 vs 0x8010ca7c = 0x80105bc0). The claim attaches "(cols 6-8: 0x80107438/0x80105bc0/NULL)" to row8 ONLY and never states 0x80105438 anywhere in row 7. Its own dump lists [70] 0x8010ca58 -> 0x80105438, so the MEANING section contradicts its own data. A port built from this spec emits 0x80105bc0 (or 0x801066fc) where the original has 0x80105438.

=== FAILURE 2: "Five distinct executors" then lists SIX ===

findings.title: Hit DIRECTION bits in ent[0x1D0]: back / left-side / right-side, exact angle sectors
findings.meaning:
phi = bearing(attack.xz -> zombie.xz) - zombie.yaw, computed with the same FUN_800154AC used by the WALK executor. 4096 = 360 deg.
  (phi+1024)&0xFFF < 2048  -> ent[0x1D0] |= 0x20   ; phi in [-1024,+1024)
  (phi+1536)&0xFFF < 1024  -> ent[0x1D0] |= 0x40   ; phi in [-1536,-512)
  (phi-512)&0xFFF  < 1024  -> ent[0x1D0] |= 0x80   ; phi in [+512,+1536)
When the zombie faces the attacker, zombie.yaw == bearing(zombie->attacker) == bearing(attacker->zombie)+2048, so phi == 2048. Shot in the back gives phi == 0. Therefore bit 0x20 = hit from BEHIND (+-90 deg), bits 0x40/0x80 = the two 90-deg SIDE sectors, and none-of-the-three = FRONT (phi in [1536,2560), i.e. +-45 deg of face-on). A duplicate of this block is at 0x80041a00-0x80041a84 in the melee path.
HURT consumes bit 0x20 to mirror the reaction (see stagger/knockdown findings) and bits 0x40/0x80 to pick which arm gets blown off.

verdict.why:
The CORE of the claim survives — I independently re-derived it and it is right — but the claim is labeled PROVEN while containing one outright invention, a listing that drops a delay slot and a jump, and a materially incomplete copy-census. Per "refuted=true if ANY part fails":

FAILURE 1 — "bits 0x40/0x80 to pick which arm gets blown off" is INVENTED. Nothing identifies a body part. The only consumer of 0x40/0x80 in the whole overlay is HURT @0x801052a4:
  801052a4: lhu v0,464(s1)
  801052ac: andi v0,v0,0xc0
  801052b0: beq v0,zero,0x801053d8
  801052b4: addiu a0,zero,9        ; DELAY SLOT
  801052b8: jal 0x8005bd6c
  801052bc: addu a1,s1,zero        ; DELAY SLOT
  801052c8: andi v0,v0,0x80
  801052cc: beq v0,zero,0x801052e8
  801052d4: lw v1,408(s1) / 801052dc: addiu s0,v1,2064 / 801052e4: ori v0,v0,0x40   (bit 0x80 set)
  801052e8: lw v1,408(s1) / 801052f0: addiu s0,v1,1548 / 801052f4: ori v0,v0,0x20   (bit 0x40 set)
  801052fc: sh v0,538(s1)
What is PROVEN: 0xC0 gates a call to EXE FUN_8005BD6C(9, ent), then bit 0x80 selects data offset ent[0x198]+0x810 & sets ent+0x21A bit 0x40, else +0x60C & bit 0x20. "Arm" appears nowhere. I checked the +0x21A readers in the draw path (8010034c `andi a3,a3,0x400`, 80100388 `andi v0,v0,0x2`) — no evidence bits 0x20/0x40 hide a limb mesh. FUN_8005BD6C indexes a table at 0x800dbb84 by (a0&0xff)*4 (8005bda8-8005bdc0), which I cannot identify either. This must be marked UNKNOWN.

FAILURE 2 — the quoted listing DROPS A DELAY SLOT and a control transfer. Real code:
  80047610: beq v0,zero,0x80047630
  80047614: addu v0,s1,zero     <-- DELAY SLOT, omitted from the claim
  80047618: lhu v0,464(s1)
  80047620: ori v0,v0,0x80
  80047624: j 0x8004742c        <-- omitted from the claim
  80047628: sh v0,464(s1)       <-- delay slot of that j, presented as straight-line
Harmless in effect (0x8004742c is `j 0x80047630` + `addu v0,s1,zero`, so both paths return s1), but the listing is not faithful.

FAILURE 3 — "A duplicate of this block is at 0x80041a00" is incomplete: there are THREE copies. The claim missed 0x80047350-0x800473d8, inside the very function it was quoting (identical `jal 0x800154ac` @0x80047358, `lh v1,118(s1)` @0x80047360, same 1024/2048, 1536/1024, -512/1024 sectors, same 0x20/0x40/0x80 at 464(s1)). A port implementing only two paths misses a live one.

FAILURE 4 — the sectors OVERLAP; the claim's summary reads as a 4-way partition. 0x20 = [-1024,1024) overlaps 0x80 = [512,1536) on [512,1024), and 0x40 = [2560,3584) on [3072,3584). This is behaviorally live: at phi=768 HURT both mirrors (0x20 test @0x8010562c) and qualifies for dismember (0xC0 test @0x801052ac).

WHAT I CONFIRMED (stronger than the claim proved it): the geometry is CORRECT.
- FUN_800154AC(a0=x_from,a1=z_from,a2=x_to,a3=z_to) — 800154c8 `subu s0,a2,a0` (dx=to-from), 800154dc `subu a0,a3,a1` (dz=to-from). So the call at 800475a8 with a0=s4[0],a1=s4[8],a2=s1[0x38],a3=s1[0x40] IS bearing(attack -> zombie).
- s4 is a position vector (x@0,y@4,z@8): 8004718c `lw a0,4(s4)` is used as a Y coord in the vertical gate 80047194-800471a4. s1 = the scanned entity (800471fc `addu s1,s0,zero`).
- The yaw convention MATCHES, via the turn helper the WALK executor already uses: FUN_80015558 does 80015584 `lh a0,56(s1)` / 80015588 `lh a1,64(s1)` -> jal 0x800154ac, i.e. bearing(self->target), then 800155dc `sh v1,118(s1)` writes that bearing straight into +0x76. So yaw == bearing(self->target) when facing.
- bearing(A->B) == bearing(B->A)+2048 exactly: 800154e0-800154e8 (dx==0 -> 1024 vs 3072) and 80015530-8001553c (base 4096 if dx>=0 else 2048; the ratio is unchanged under negation because MIPS `div` truncates toward zero).
=> phi == 2048 face-on, phi == 0 from behind. Bit 0x20 = BACK is CORRECT.
- Low byte of +0x1D0 is per-candidate scratch: 8004717c `andi v1,v1,0xff00` + 80047184 `sh v1,464(s0)` clears it; 80047200 `ori v0,v0,0x1` = hit confirmed.

verdict.correction:
KEEP the sector decoding — it is correct and now properly proven. Restate it as:

phi = FUN_800154AC(attack.x, attack.z, zombie.x, zombie.z) - (s16)zombie[0x76], 4096 = 360 deg.
PROVEN direction: FUN_800154AC returns the bearing FROM (a0,a1) TO (a2,a3) — 800154c8 `subu s0,a2,a0`, 800154dc `subu a0,a3,a1`. So phi is measured from the ATTACK POINT toward the ZOMBIE.

Therefore +0x76 is in the same angular frame, and yaw == bearing(zombie->attacker) when the zombie faces the attacker.

Flags, written to the LOW byte of ent+0x1D0 (halfword access, lhu/sh), NON-EXCLUSIVE — evaluate all three independently, do NOT use else-if:
  if (((phi + 1024) & 0xFFF) < 2048) ent[0x1D0] |= 0x20;   // BACK  half-plane, +-90 deg   @800475bc-800475d8
  if (((phi + 1536) & 0xFFF) < 1024) ent[0x1D0] |= 0x40;   // SIDE-A quadrant, phi [2560,3584)  @800475cc-800475fc
  if (((phi -  512) & 0xFFF) < 1024) ent[0x1D0] |= 0x80;   // SIDE-B quadrant, phi [ 512,1536)  @800475f0-80047620

Which of 0x40 / 0x80 is the zombie's LEFT vs RIGHT is UNKNOWN — it depends on the handedness of the atan table at FUN_8008D190, which I did not decode. Label them SIDE-A / SIDE-B until that is resolved.

THREE identical copies exist, all must be ported:
  1. 0x80047350-0x800473d8  (FUN_800470c0, first hit path)  — bearing call @0x80047358
  2. 0x800475a0-0x80047628  (FUN_800470c0, second hit path) — bearing call @0x800475a8

findings.title: Generic STAGGER executor 0x80105438 — 4 phases in ent[0x6], driven by a PROCEDURAL torso bend, not a clip
findings.meaning:
switch(ent[0x6]): 0 -> 0x801054bc (enter), 1 -> 0x8010573c (hold), 2 -> 0x8010588c (unbend), 3 -> 0x80105a50 (exit decision), default -> end.
Phase 0: if ent[0x218] != ent[0x14C] then ent[0x14C] = 0x000F0000 + ent[0x218] (motion request, bank 0xF); voice: if ent[0x239]==0 play sound id 11 or 12 (rand&1) via 0x8005BD6C then ent[0x239]=150; gait ent[0x16B] = 24; two calls to 0x80015E7C with ent[0x14D] temporarily zeroed; ent[0x6]=1, ent[0x15A]=1, ent[0x158]=0; cooldown decrement (separate finding); if (ent[0x1D0]&0x20) { ent[0x15A] = -1; blood_yaw_bias = 2048; }  <- mirrored bend + 180-deg blood spray for a hit from behind.
Phases 0/1/2 all build a rotation vector { 0, 0, -8 * ent[0x158] * ent[0x16B] * ent[0x15A] } (phase 2 uses the non-negated form), turn it into a matrix with 0x8008E1F4 (RotMatrix), and MULTIPLY it into TWO model matrices: ent[0x198]+24 (0x8008D934) and ent[0x198]+172+24 (0x8008DA44). That is a runtime spine/torso twist layered on top of the motion — a hit reaction that bends the body by an amount proportional to a counter, in a direction taken from the hit angle.
Phase 1 counts ent[0x158] up; at >= 3 it sets ent[0x6]=2 and ent[0x158]=16. Phase 2 counts ent[0x158] DOWN and at 0 sets ent[0x6]=3.

verdict.why:
I re-disassembled 0x80105438-0x80105bc0 from EMZ0.BIN myself. The 4-phase skeleton is real (dispatch, delay slots, and most cited constants check out), but the claim's central characterization of the "procedural bend" is FALSE, and it contains a delay-slot misread plus two omissions that would break a byte-true port.

=== FATAL #1: "(phase 2 uses the non-negated form)" is BACKWARDS, and the x8 scale does NOT exist in phase 2 ===
Every phase builds TWO vectors, one negated and one not. The real difference between phase 0/1 and phase 2 is the <<3 scale, which phase 2 LACKS entirely.

phase0/1 block A @0x801057b8:
  801057b8: mflo t0
  801057bc: sll v0,t0,3        <- x8
  801057c0: subu v0,zero,v0    <- NEGATED
  801057c4: mult v0,v1         => z = -8*A*B*C
phase0/1 block B @0x80105804:
  80105804: lh v0,346(s1)
  80105808: mflo t0
  8010580c: sll v0,v0,3        <- x8
  80105814: mult t0,v0         => z = +8*A*B*C
phase2 block A @0x801058e4:
  801058e4: mflo t0
  801058e8: lh v1,346(s1)
  801058ec: subu v0,zero,t0    <- NEGATED, directly from t0, NO sll
  801058f0: mult v0,v1         => z = -1*A*B*C
phase2 block B @0x80105930:
  80105930: mflo t0
  80105934: lh v0,346(s1)
  80105938: nop
  8010593c: mult t0,v0         <- NO sll  => z = +1*A*B*C

Byte proof (the `sll` word c0 10 08 00 / c0 10 02 00 is simply absent in phase 2):
  0x801057a4: 58 01 23 86 | 6b 01 22 82 | 00 00 00 00 | 18 00 62 00 | 5a 01 23 86 | 12 40 00 00 | c0 10 08 00 | 23 10 02 00 | 18 00 43 00
  0x801058d4: 58 01 23 86 | 6b 01 22 82 | 00 00 00 00 | 18 00 62 00 | 12 40 00 00 | 5a 01 23 86 | 23 10 08 00 | 18 00 43 00
So the claim's constant "bend scale <<3 (x8) @0x801057bc", presented as the bend scale, is only true for phases 0/1. A port following the claim bends 8x too far for the whole unbend phase and puts the wrong sign on one of the two matrices.

=== FATAL #2: "gait ent[0x16B] = 24 @0x80105514" is overwritten to 2 ===
  80105510: lbu v1,5(s1)
  80105514: addiu v0,zero,24
  80105518: sb v0,363(s1)          ; = 24
  8010551c: addiu v0,zero,16
  80105520: bne v1,v0,0x80105580   ; ent[5] != 16 -> skip
  80105524: addu a0,s1,zero        ; DELAY SLOT
  ...
  8010556c: addiu v1,zero,2
  80105570: sb v1,363(s1)          ; ent[0x16B] = 2 when ent[5]==16
ent[0x16B] is read as a direct multiplicand of the bend (`801057a8: lb v0,363(s1)`), so this is a 12x magnitude error for sub_state 16. The claim states 24 flatly.

=== DELAY-SLOT ERROR: "two calls to 0x80015E7C with ent[0x14D] temporarily zeroed" ===
  80105588: lbu s0,333(s1)
  80105590: jal 0x80015e7c
  80105594: sb zero,333(s1)   ; DELAY SLOT -> call #1 sees 0
  801055a8: jal 0x80015e7c
  801055ac: sb s0,333(s1)     ; DELAY SLOT -> executes BEFORE the call
Only the FIRST call runs with ent[0x14D]==0; the SECOND runs with the ORIGINAL value restored. The claim's wording says both.

=== OMISSION: the executor's entry gate is missing entirely ===
  80105444: addiu a0,zero,1
  80105458: lbu v0,546(s1)
  80105460: bne v0,a0,0x80105478
  80105468: jal 0x80105bc0
  8010546c: addu a0,s1,zero
  80105470: j 0x80105ba0
If ent[0x222]==1 the whole 4-phase machine is BYPASSED for handler 0x80105bc0. Also 0x80105b84 is not "end": it is `lbu v1,536(s1) / lbu v0,332(s1) / bne v1,v0,0x80105ba0 / jal 0x800152c8(ent,0)` before the epilogue at 0x80105ba0.

=== OTHER DEFECTS ===
- Phase-2 exit: `80105970: bne v1,zero,0x80105980` with delay slot `80105974: sh v0,344(s1)` stores v1-1 UNCONDITIONALLY, so on the exit tick ent[0x158] = 0xFFFF, not 0. Claim says "at 0 sets ent[0x6]=3" with no mention.
- "blood_yaw_bias" is UNPROVEN invention. s3 is a saved register whose entry value is `8010545c: lw s3,496(s1)` (= ent[0x1F0]) and which phase 2 reuses as a distance test `80105980: sltiu v0,s3,0x514`. In phase 0 it is zeroed (`801055c8: addu s3,zero,zero`) and set to 2048 (`8010563c: addiu s3,zero,2048`), then consumed as `801056d0/80105700: subu a1,v0,a1` (yaw MINUS bias, not "+2048") into 0x8001bf10(a0=6096,...). Most of the control flow re-derives exactly (switch + delay slots, phase-0 writes, fall-through, phase-advance-on-motion-end, phase-2 delay-slot sw 257, latch/cooldown behaviour). But FOUR parts are contradicted by instructions, and the claim is marked PROVEN.

(1) "bank 3" is INVENTED — the high half of the motion word is the CROSSFADE-STEP COUNTER, not an animation bank. 0x8002959c->0x80029614 reads it: `800296a8: lbu t3,334(s2)` (334 = 0x14E), `800296b0: beq t3,zero,0x8002973c` (0 => no interpolation), `800296b8: andi v0,a3,0xffff` / `800296bc: mult v0,t3` / `800296e4: addiu v0,zero,4096` / `800296ec: subu v0,v0,t1` (a3=1024, t3=3 => weight 4096-3072=1024) feeding the GTE block, and it is DECREMENTED at `800299c0: lbu v0,334(s2)` / `800299c8: addiu v0,v0,-1` / `800299cc: sb v0,334(s2)`. So writing 0x00030004 arms a 3-step, 1024-per-step crossfade; the a3=1024 the claim treats as an opaque constant is that step size. The claim's parenthetical "[the motion stepper reading ent[0x14C]/ent[0x14D]]" also omits this read of ent[0x14E].

(2) "Root pitch ent[0x144] = -450" is INVENTED and contradicted. +0x144/+0x148 are the 8-byte parameter block handed to the effect spawner: `80105fac: addiu a3,s4,324` and `80105fe0: addiu a3,s4,324`, then `80105ff4: jal 0x8001bf10`, and the callee consumes a3 as a pointer — `8001bfe0: beq a3,zero,0x8001c000` / `8001bfe8: lw v0,0(a3)` / `8001bff0: sw v0,44(t0)` / `8001bff4: lw v0,4(a3)` / `8001bffc: sw v0,48(t0)` (zeroed when a3==0). findings.title: ARM DISMEMBERMENT is inside HURT, gated by a per-limb HP byte ent[0x152], not by the flinch cooldown
findings.meaning:
Condition to blow an arm off: !(ent[0x21A] & 0x60) && (int8)ent[0x152] < 0 && (ent[0x1D0] & 0xC0).
ent[0x151]/[0x152]/[0x153] are THREE limb HP bytes, each initialised to 13 (0x80100820-0x80100828 and again at 0x801049b8-0x801049c0), decremented by a 3-bit per-hit amount and clamped at exactly -1 (0x80041938-0x80041944, 0x8004197c-0x80041988, 0x800419bc-0x800419cc). Side bit 0x80 picks the model part at ent[0x198]+2064, bit 0x40 picks ent[0x198]+1548, and the corresponding ent[0x21A] bit (0x40 / 0x20) is latched so it can only happen once per side.
The swap copies four pointers from ent[0x198]+2588/2592/2596/2600 into part+8/12/16/20 (unless ent[8]==30) and ORs 0x1062 into the flags of part+172 — a real mesh substitution, plus two 0x8001BF10 gore emitters (types 8000 and 7000) with a randomised yaw, and voice id 9.

verdict.why:
I re-disassembled every cited address in C:\workspace\git\reAi_v2\info\re2leon\COMMON\BIN\EMZ0.BIN and C:\workspace\git\reAi_v2\info\re2leon\PSX.EXE and verified raw bytes. The INSTRUCTIONS are transcribed correctly and every DELAY SLOT in the claim's listing is correctly assigned (I found no delay-slot error). What fails is the MEANING, on six independent points.

(1) THE GATE IS INCOMPLETE — the block is unreachable unless (ent[0x21A] & 0x2)==0.
0x80105280 is `j 0x80105418` (unconditional), so 0x80105288 is a pure branch target and v1 is NOT set locally. Grepping the ENTIRE overlay, 0x80105288 has exactly ONE predecessor:
  80105168: lhu v1,538(s1)
  80105170: andi v0,v1,0x2
  80105174: beq v0,zero,0x80105288      (delay slot 80105178: addiu v0,zero,1)
This also proves v1 = ent[0x21A] (so the &0x60 gate itself is right). But the claim's stated condition "!(ent[0x21A]&0x60) && (int8)ent[0x152]<0 && (ent[0x1D0]&0xC0)" omits the mandatory (ent[0x21A]&0x2)==0. A port using the claim's condition fires dismemberment where the original provably cannot.

(2) THE MESH SWAP IS A 50/50 COIN FLIP, NOT "unless ent[8]==30".
  801052f8: jal 0x80015fe8              ; PRNG
  801052fc: sh v0,538(s1)               ; DELAY SLOT — stores the latch; v0 after return = PRNG result
  80105300: andi v0,v0,0x1
  80105304: beq v0,zero,0x80105354      (delay slot 80105308: addiu v0,zero,30)
Raw bytes confirm: 801052f8: fa 57 00 0c | 1a 02 22 a6 | 01 00 42 30 | 13 00 40 10 | 1e 00 02 24.
So the four-pointer copy runs only when (rand&1)!=0 AND ent[8]!=30. The claim names ONLY the ent[8]==30 exception. Worse, 0x80105354 IS the branch target, so the two 0x8001bf10 emitters and the `ori v0,v0,0x1062` at 0x8010537c ALWAYS run while the mesh substitution runs half the time — so "a real mesh substitution" mischaracterises the block.

(3) "ARM" IS INVENTED. I proved the part array is ent[0x198] + 172*n:
  8010514c: lw s0,408(s1) / 80105158: addiu a2,s0,72     -> part[0]+72 (position field)
  801050f4: lw a2,408(s1) / 80105110: addiu a2,a2,244    -> part[1]+72 (172+72)
  reset walk: addiu a0,a0,176 / 348 / 520 / ... / 2412   -> 172n+4 for n=1..14 (15 parts, 0..14)
Therefore s0=2064=172*12 -> part[12] then part[13]; s0=1548=172*9 -> part[9] then part[10]; source 2588/2592/2596/2600 = part[15]+8/12/16/20 (a spare part beyond the 15-bone skeleton). NO instruction anywhere identifies these as arms. In the conventional Capcom 15-bone layout indices 9-11 / 12-14 are the LEG chains and 3-8 are the arms — so the evidence points away from "arm". info/re2leon contains no room/EMD data, so the bone names cannot be settled here. This must be UNKNOWN, not PROVEN.

(4) THE "SIDE BIT" IS A HIT-BEARING QUADRANT, NOT A LIMB SIDE. ent[0x1D0]'s bits are written in PSX.EXE from the shot bearing relative to the zombie's own yaw:
  800419f0: jal 0x800154ac        (bearing helper)
  80041a00: lh v1,118(t0)         (ent[0x76] = yaw)
  80041a08: subu v1,v0,v1
  80041a0c: addiu v0,v1,1024 / 80041a10: andi v0,v0,0xfff / 80041a14: slti v0,v0,2048 -> 80041a28: ori v0,v0,0x20
  80041a30: addiu v0,v1,1536 / 80041a34: andi / 80041a38: slti v0,v0,1024            -> 80041a54: ori v0,v0,0x40
  80041a5c: addiu v0,v1,-512  / 80041a60: andi / 80041a64: slti v0,v0,1024            -> 80041a80: ori v0,v0,0x80
So 0x40/0x80 are 90-degree direction-of-hit quadrants and a THIRD bit 0x20 (front 180 degrees) shares the field — which is precisely why the mask at 0x801052ac is 0xC0 and not 0xE0. The claim presents 0x80/0x40 as unexplained magic.

(5) "THREE LIMB HP BYTES" IS A LABEL, NOT A PROOF, AND ONLY ONE IS READ HERE. The selector is 112(sp)=s7 (0x8004176c: sw s7,112(sp)), and s7 comes from a data table, not a limb id:
  80041484: addu a0,v0,s0        ; a0 = 0x800a6db4 + s1*9 + s0
  80041488: lbu v1,2(a0) / 80041490: and v0,v1,s6 / 80041494: beq v0,zero,0x800414a8 / 8010549c: srl s7,v1,1
Table 0x800a6db4 = 04 02 01 02 01 04 01 02 04 04 02 00 02 00 00 01 02 00 ... i.e. bitmasks {1,2,4} -> s7 {0,1,2}. So these are three damage-GROUP HP bytes keyed by a hit-region mask. Confirmed selector routing: s7==0 -> ent[0x153] (0x80041928), ==1 -> ent[0x152] (0x8004196c), ==2 -> ent[0x151] (0x800419b0). The dismemberment block reads ONLY ent[0x152]; 0x151/0x153 are never read by it.

(6) "NOT BY THE FLINCH COOLDOWN" IS FALSE AS STATED. The dismemberment check is skipped entirely whenever the routine takes the flinch/blood-spray block at 0x801050a0, because BOTH of its exits are unconditional returns: 0x80105114 `j 0x80105418` and 0x8010515c `j 0x80105418` (0x80105418 = `lw ra,40(sp)`, the epilogue). Entry to that block is 0x80105064 `bne v0,zero,0x80105168` (ent[6]), 0x80105078 `bne v0,zero,0x80105168` (slt v1,(int8)ent[0x223]), 0x80105088 `beq v0,v1,0x801050a0` (ent[0x222]==1), 0x80105098 `bne v0,v1,0x80105164` (ent[5]!=1) — and ent[0x223] is itself a randomized 16..31 counter (0x801050c0: andi v0,v0,0xf / 0x801050c4: addiu v0,v0,16 / 0x801050c8: sb v0,547(s1)). So dismemberment is absolutely control-flow-dependent on that timer logic.

Minor: "voice id 9" — a0=9 is real (0x801052b4, delay slot of the branch at 0x801052b0, so it is also set on the taken path, harmless because 0x801053d8 `addu a0,s1,zero` overwrites it), but 0x8005bd6c is never shown to be a voice routine: UNKNOWN. Also the claim cites the re-init as "0x801049b8-0x801049c0" but the `addiu v0,zero,13` is at 0x801049b4; the cited range holds only the three `sb` stores.

CORRECTLY VERIFIED parts of the claim: 0x80105294 `lb v0,338(s1)` is a SIGNED load and 0x8010529c `bgez v0,0x801053e0` requires it < 0 (bytes 52 01 22 82 / 50 00 41 04); the 0xC0 test at 0x801052ac/0x801052b0; bit 0x80 -> +2064 + latch 0x40 and else +1548 + latch 0x20 at 0x801052c8-0x801052f4; the init to 13 at 0x8010081c-0x80100828; and the -1 saturation at 0x8004197c-0x80041988 (plus the sibling blocks 0x80041938-0x80041944 and 0x800419c0-0x800419cc).

verdict.why:
The instruction BYTES and the delay-slot assignments in the claim are correct, and the context (phase 2, s3 = ent[0x1F0]) checks out — but three of its cited facts fail, one of them a fabricated constant that would break a byte-true port.

WHAT I CONFIRMED (so the true part is not lost):
- Function start 0x80105438; `8010545c: lw s3,496(s1)` => s3 = ent[0x1F0]. I scanned 0x8010545c..0x80105a40 on the taken path: NO write to s3. Claim CORRECT.
- Phase dispatch `80105478: lbu v1,6(s1)` then `801054a0: addiu v0,zero,2 / 801054a4: beq v1,v0,0x8010588c / 801054a8: addiu v0,zero,3 (delay slot) / 801054ac: beq v1,v0,0x80105a50`. 0x8010588c..0x80105980 is straight-line (only branch is `80105970: bne v1,zero,0x80105980`, delay slot `80105974: sh v0,344(s1)`), so 0x80105980 DOES execute every frame in phase 2. Claim CORRECT.
- Delay slots all correct, incl. the tricky `80105a08: bne v0,zero,0x80105a14 / 80105a0c: addiu v0,zero,769 (delay slot) / 80105a10: sw v0,4(s1)` — the bne tests the jal return value, the delay slot then overwrites v0 with 769. Claim CORRECT.
- 769 = 0x0301 -> +4=1(ACTIVE), +5=3; corroborated by the same word-store idiom at `8010517c: lui v1,0x6 / 80105180: ori v1,v1,0x501 / 80105184: sw v1,4(s1)`.

FAILURE 1 (FATAL, cited constant is a tool artifact): the claim lists "0x800CFE65" for the first reach call. `801059f4: addiu a1,a1,-411` — raw bytes at 0x801059f4 are `65 fe a5 24` = 0x24A5FE65, i.e. rs=a1, rt=a1: it is CHAINED on the existing a1, which was set to 0x800CFDCB by `8010598c: lui a1,0x800d / 80105990: addiu a1,a1,-565`. No instruction between them writes a1, and I scanned the whole overlay for any branch/jump into 0x801059f4 — there are NONE. So a1 = 0x800CFDCB - 411 = 0x800CFC30, the SAME pointer as the second call (`80105a28: lui a1,0x800d / 80105a2c: addiu a1,a1,-976` = 0x800CFC30). 0x800CFE65 is 0x800D0000-411, i.e. exactly the disassembler's naive lui-only annotation. Proof the annotation column is unreliable: at `80105994: lbu v0,0(a1)` the tool prints "0x800d0000" although a1 = 0x800CFDCB — the claim silently corrected THAT one but copied the bogus one. The claim's whole "two different reach targets" structure is invented; both calls test the same target, which is the player position (words at 0x800CFC30/0x800CFC38 are loaded as x/z and fed to the turn helper at `80105a70: lw a1,-976(a1) / 80105a78: lw a2,-968(a2) / 80105a7c: jal 0x80015614` and at `801026e8/801026f0 -> 801026f4: jal 0x80015558`).

FAILURE 2: "reach radius 288" is a misreading of FUN_80015758. Its tail is `800157ac: andi v0,v0,0xfff / 800157b0: sll s0,s0,1 / 800157b4: sltu v0,v0,s0 / 800157b8: xori v0,v0,0x1` after `80015788: jal 0x800154ac` (bearing). a3=288 is an ANGULAR half-width in 12-bit yaw units (288/4096 = 25.3 deg), tested against a 0xFFF-masked angle difference. There is no distance term anywhere in it. 288 is not a radius.

FAILURE 3: "the two ent[0x21A] guards (0x20/0x40) are exactly the two ARM-BLOWN-OFF latches ... a zombie whose left arm is gone cannot reach with that arm" is contradicted by every writer of those bits. They are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE — exactly one is ever set: `80105e40: jal 0x80015fe8 (PRNG) / 80105e50: lhu v1,538(s4) / 80105e54: andi s0,s0,0x1 / 80105e58: ori v1,v1,0x20 / 80105e5c: beq s0,zero,0x80105e70 / 80105e60: sh v1,538(s4) (delay slot) / 80105e64: andi v0,v1,0xffdf / 80105e68: ori v0,v0,0x40 / 80105e6c: sh v0,538(s4)` — sets 0x20, then on a COIN FLIP clears 0x20 and sets 0x40. findings.title: Crawler and already-flinching zombies bypass the whole reaction system
findings.meaning:
1) If ent[0x10E] & 0x1 (the crawling variant), HURT jumps straight to a FLAT table @0x8010CBE8 indexed by routine_1 alone — no zone, no cooldown, no latch. Entry [0] is NULL, every other entry [1..18] is the single handler 0x80107888. Note the `j 0x8010540c` at 0x8010500c lands on the `nop` before the shared `jalr v0` tail, and the delay slot 0x80105010 sets a0 = entity.
2) If ent[0x21A] & 0x10, HURT tail-calls 0x80107A78 and returns (0x8010501c-0x80105038) — again bypassing the cooldown, latch and 2D table entirely. That bit is set at 0x8010358c and cleared at 0x801036bc, both inside the executor of ACTIVE substate 5 (0x80103188..0x8010394b) — i.e. this is the 'hit again while already playing the light flinch' path.
3) If ent[0x21A] & 0x2 (set at 0x801032e4 / 0x80104094 via `ori 0x202`, cleared at 0x801036cc), the body takes the 0x8010517c branch: routine word = 0x00060501 (ACTIVE, routine_1 = 5, routine_3 = 6), gait ent[0x16B] = 1, per-substate calls to 0x80106128 / 0x80106310 / 0x8010640C / 0x80106510 for routine_1 == 10 / 11 / 9 / 14 / 16, and RETURNS without ever reaching the 2D dispatch.

verdict.why:
Parts 1 and 3 survive re-disassembly essentially intact, but part 2's EXCLUSIVITY claim — the one that carries the whole "already-flinching" identification — is FALSE, and part 3's setter list is incomplete. Both were labelled PROVEN.

=== WHAT I CONFIRMED (instruction-for-instruction) ===

(a) Crawler bypass — every quoted instruction is exact:
  80104fe0: lhu a0,270(s1)
  80104fe8: andi v0,a0,0x1
  80104fec: beq v0,zero,0x80105014
  80104ff0: addu a1,s2,zero        <- delay slot, always runs (correctly assigned)
  80104ff4: lbu v0,5(s1)
  80104ffc: sll v0,v0,2
  80105008: lw v0,-13336(at)       0x8010cbe8
  8010500c: j 0x8010540c
  80105010: addu a0,s1,zero        <- delay slot, correctly assigned
The tail is as described:
  801053e0..80105408 = the 2D dispatch (base 0x8010c940, stride 9*4, +ent[0x1D2]*4)
  8010540c: nop                    <- the j lands here, skipping the 2D computation
  80105410: jalr v0
  80105414: addu a2,s3,zero        <- delay slot
Table verified: 8010cbe8 = 00 00 00 00 (NULL); 8010cbec..8010cc30 = 88 78 10 80 (0x80107888) for indices 1..18; 8010cc34 = 09 0f 0f 23 (not a pointer) ends it. Exactly as claimed.
The "crawler" reading is also supported, which I checked independently: 8010115c: andi v0,v0,0x3f / 8010116c: lw v0,-14252(at) (0x8010c854); that table has 14 entries alternating 8c 11 10 80 / 10 12 10 80 = 0x8010118c (even) / 0x80101210 (odd) up to 0x8010c888, so bit0 of (+0x10E & 0x3F) does select the crawl variant.

(b) The bit-0x10 early-out itself and its delay slots are correct:
  80105014: lhu v0,538(s1)
  8010501c: andi v0,v0,0x10
  80105020: beq v0,zero,0x8010503c
  80105024: andi v0,a0,0x40        <- delay slot, always runs (claim's ranges are consistent with this)
  8010502c: jal 0x80107a78
  80105030: addu a2,s3,zero        <- delay slot
  80105034: j 0x80105418           (epilogue)

(c) Part 3's mechanics: 80105170: andi v0,v1,0x2 / 80105174: beq v0,zero,0x80105288 / 80105178: addiu v0,zero,1 (delay slot) — so bit set = fall through to 0x8010517c. Then 8010517c: lui v1,0x6 / 80105180: ori v1,v1,0x501 / 80105184: sw v1,4(s1) = 0x00060501, and 8010518c: sb v0,363(s1) (0x16B = 1, v0 from the delay slot). And it does return without the 2D dispatch: 8010522c: bne v1,v0,0x80105418 and 80105280: j 0x80105418 are the only exits.

=== WHAT REFUTES IT ===

REFUTATION 1 (fatal to the "already playing the light flinch" identification). The claim states: "That bit is set at 0x8010358c and cleared at 0x801036bc, both inside the executor of ACTIVE substate 5 (0x80103188..0x8010394b) — i.e. this is the 'hit again while already playing the light flinch' path."
Bit 0x10 is ALSO set inside the executor of ACTIVE substate 8:
  80103d00: lhu v0,538(s1)
  80103d08: ori v0,v0,0x10
  80103d0c: bne v1,zero,0x80103d60
  80103d10: sh v0,538(s1)          <- DELAY SLOT of the bne => the store ALWAYS executes
s1 is the entity there: 80103b7c: addu s1,a0,zero (executor 8 prologue). Executor table @0x8010c8cc gives [8]=0x80103b74, [9]=0x80103e48, so 0x80103d10 is squarely inside substate 8, NOT substate 5.
The same executor also clears it twice, both in delay slots:
  80103d84: andi v0,v0,0xffef / 80103d88: j 0x80103e24 / 80103d8c: sh v0,538(s1)
  80103da4: andi v1,v1,0xffef / 80103dac: j 0x80103e24 / 80103db0: sh v1,538(s1)
So ent[0x21A] bit 0x10 is not a substate-5 ("light flinch") marker. A port built on this claim would fire the 0x80107a78 early-out in the wrong state.

REFUTATION 2. The clear list is also wrong-by-omission: bit 0x10 is additionally cleared at
  80103748: andi v1,v1,0xffed / 80103750: sh v1,538(s2)   (clears 0x10 AND 0x2 together — executor 5 epilogue)
  80107ea0: andi v1,v1,0xffed / 80107ea4: sh v1,538(s1)   (outside every ACTIVE executor, in the 0x80107a78..0x80107ef0 reaction-handler region)

REFUTATION 3. "ent[0x21A] & 0x2 (set at 0x801032e4 / 0x80104094 via ori 0x202, cleared at 0x801036cc)" — there are at least two more setters:
  80102dbc: ori v1,v1,0x202 / 80102dc4: jal 0x80015fe8 / 80102dc8: sh v1,538(s1)  <- DELAY SLOT, always runs. s1 = entity (801025f4: addu s1,a0,zero). Inside executor 3 (table [3]=0x801025ec, [4]=0x80103178).
  80104438: andi v0,v0,0xfffb / 8010443c: ori v0,v0,0x2 / 80104448: sh v0,538(s0). s0 = entity (801043a4: addu s0,a0,zero). Inside executor 11 (table [11]=0x8010439c, [12]=0x80104748).
And it is cleared at 0x80103750 too, not only at 0x801036cc.

=== SMALLER ERRORS ===
- "routine word = 0x00060501 (ACTIVE, routine_1 = 5, routine_3 = 6)": sw v1,4(s1) little-endian puts 0x01->ent+4, 0x05->ent+5, 0x06->ent+6, 0x00->ent+7. Under the project's own convention (+0x5 = sub_state_1), the 6 lands in ent+6, i.e. routine_2, not routine_3.
- "calls to 0x80106128 / 0x80106310 / 0x8010640C / 0x80106510 for routine_1 == 10 / 11 / 9 / 14 / 16" pairs 5 values against 4 functions and omits the guards. Actual: 10->0x80106128 gated on !(ent[0x10E]&0x80) (801051a4: andi v0,v0,0x80 / 801051a8: bne v0,zero,0x801051c8) then sets ent[0x21A]|=0x800 (801051c0/801051c4); 11->0x80106310 ungated; 9->0x8010640c gated on !(ent[0x10E]&0x80) (801051f8/801051fc); 14->0x80106510 ungated; 16->0x80106128 gated on !(ent[0x10E]&0x80) (8010523c/80105240) AND ent[0x23A] >= 9 (80105248: lbu v0,570(s1) / 80105250: sltiu v0,v0,0x9 / 80105254: bne v0,zero,0x80105274), then sets |=0x800 (8010526c/80105270) and always increments ent[0x23A] (8010527c: addiu v0,v0,1 / 80105284: sb v0,570(s1), delay slot of j 0x80105418).

NOT a refutation but worth flagging: with the crawler bit set and routine_1 == 0, 0x8010500c jumps to the jalr with v0 = NULL from 0x8010cbe8[0] — an unguarded call to address 0. The claim notes entry [0] is NULL but does not note that nothing guards it.

findings.meaning:
Things a naive 'play a flinch clip' port would get wrong:
1. The stagger has NO dedicated animation for the bend. It requests a motion (ent[0x14C] = 0x000F0000|ent[0x218], i.e. the CURRENT motion re-requested) and then rotates two model matrices by -8*ent[0x158]*ent[0x16B]*ent[0x15A] every frame, ramping up over 3 frames and back down over 16. The sign comes from the hit direction. The zombie keeps walking underneath.
2. There are TWO reactions selected by a persistent latch (ent[0x222]), not by the hit itself: stagger 0x80105438 vs knockdown 0x80105bc0. The latch survives across hits and is only cleared on get-up, and only if the cooldown has expired.
3. Stagger duration is a fixed frame counter (up to 3, down from 16). Knockdown duration is the MOTION length — phase advances only when 0x8002959C returns 1.
4. Recovery is a randomised decision that can go straight to an attack substate (0x0B01 / 0x0C01 / 0x0201 / 0x0101 / 0x00010101), and phase 2 of the stagger can convert into a GRAB (0x0301) mid-reaction.
5. The flinch cooldown is arithmetic, not boolean: a per-reaction-id subtraction (9 / 15 / 15 / 35 / 20) from a random 16..31 pool, so 'how many hits before it goes down' depends on the weapon class.
6. Hit direction produces a MIRRORED reaction (bend sign, blood yaw +2048, knockdown motion 3 vs 4, root pitch -450 vs 0), and side hits with a depleted limb-HP byte replace arm meshes and permanently disable that arm's grab reach.
7. The reaction id (table row) and the hit zone (table column) come from the ATTACK, stamped by the EXE into ent[0x5] and ent[0x1D2] before HURT ever runs. The overlay never chooses them.
openQuestions: The four remaining executors 0x80107438 (zone-0 / high-hit), 0x801066fc (rows 7/8 col1), 0x8010703c (row 12 col1, itself a 7-entry jump table @0x80100104), 0x80107ef0 (rows 15/18, uses a data block @0x80100124) and the two bypass handlers 0x80107888 (crawler) / 0x80107A78 (re-hit) were only opened far enough to confirm they use the SAME ent[0x6] phase switch. Their bodies are not yet disassembled — that is the next chunk of work.
ent[0x10E] bit 0x40 (halves the flinch resistance) and bit 0x80 (suppresses several 0x80106128 / 0x8010640C calls) are set outside EMZ0, by the EXE spawn path. Their source in room data is UNKNOWN.

Globals 0x800CFBFC / 0x800CFDAC / 0x800CFDCB / 0x800CFDB8 / 0x800CFBF8 in the HURT preamble (0x80104f58-0x80104fdc: if [0x800CFBFC]==5 && [0x800CFDAC]==this, set [0x800CFBFC]=1, clear bit 0x80 of [0x800CFDCB], clear bits 0x12 of [0x800CFDB8], clear 0x1004 from ent[0] and [0x800CFBF8]) look like cancelling an in-progress grab/cutscene owned by this zombie, but I did not find the writer of 0x800CFBFC — UNKNOWN.

verdict.why:
Independently re-disassembled every cited address in EMZ0.BIN and PSX.EXE. The addresses are real, but four of the seven "PROVEN" meaning-bullets are wrong at the instruction level, and two more carry no evidence at all.

(A) BEND SCALE IS PHASE-1-ONLY. Claim: "rotates two model matrices by -8*ent[0x158]*ent[0x16B]*ent[0x15A] every frame, ramping up over 3 frames and back down over 16". Phase 1 (0x801057b0-0x801057c4) does have the shift: "801057bc: sll v0,t0,3 / 801057c0: subu v0,zero,v0". But phase 2 (sub_state_2==2 handler @0x8010588c, i.e. the entire 17-frame decay) has NO shift: "801058e0: mult v1,v0 / 801058e4: mflo t0 / 801058ec: subu v0,zero,t0 / 801058f0: mult v0,v1". Up-ramp renders 0, 8, 16; decay then starts at 16*1 (continuous). A port using the claimed formula overshoots the bend by 8x for the whole decay.

(B) SECOND MATRIX IS NOT NEGATED. "80105804: lh v0,346(s1) / 8010580c: sll v0,v0,3 / 80105814: mult t0,v0" — no subu anywhere, i.e. +8*A*B*C, opposite sign to matrix 1. Same in phase 2: "80105934: lh v0,346(s4) / 8010593c: mult t0,v0". The two matrices counter-rotate; the claim states one sign for both.

(C) THE TWO CALLS ARE DIFFERENT libgte FUNCTIONS WITH REVERSED OPERAND ORDER, not "MulMatrix" twice. Diffing the bodies: 0x8008d934 stores into a0 ("sw t6,0(a0)", "sw t0,4(a0)", "sw t1,8(a0)", "sw t8,12(a0)", "addu v0,a0,zero") = MulMatrix (m0=m0*m1); 0x8008da44 stores into a1 ("sw t6,0(a1)" ... "addu v0,a1,zero") = MulMatrix2 (m1=m0*m1). Call 1 "801057e0: addiu a0,s2,24 / 801057e4: jal 0x8008d934" computes M*R into ent[0x198]+24; call 2 "80105830: addu a0,s0,zero / 80105834: jal 0x8008da44 / 80105838: addiu a1,s2,24" computes R*M into ent[0x198]+172+24. Matrix product is non-commutative, so the spec as written produces a different pose.

(D) COOLDOWN DRAIN TABLE IS MIS-STATED. "801055d0: lui at,0x8011 / 801055d4: addu at,at,v0 / 801055d8: lbu v1,-13261(at)" gives base 0x8010CC33 + ent[0x5]. Bytes 8010cc28: 88 78 10 80 88 78 10 80 88 78 10 80 09 0f 0f 23 / 8010cc38: 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 14 00 ... So idx0 = 0x8010CC33 = 0x80 (128) and it is the top byte of the pointer 0x80107888 at 0x8010CC30; idx1..4 = 9/15/15/35; idx5..7 = 0; idx8 = 20. The claimed contiguous five-entry list "9/15/15/35/20" cannot be indexed by ent[0x5].

(E) "LATCH ONLY CLEARED ON GET-UP" IS FALSE.
